compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py::test_review_plan_start_returns_a_handle_fast_then_polls_to_passed` asserts a wall-clock bound: `review_plan_start` must return in under 2 s (`assert holder["elapsed"] < 2`, line 424, inside `anyio.fail_after(3)` at line 415). On 2026-11-03 it failed locally at `assert 2.591... < 2` ("async start must return a handle without blocking on the gate") during a `pytest -n 4` run on a host at load average 29-38, with the gate stubbed. Run alone on the same host it passed. The bound was already widened once under `jeanlike-hick-azurevase`.

The bound exists to protect the async-start contract (AGENTS.md: `review_plan_start` returns a handle "in ms on a background daemon" instead of running the gate in the request). The test's stub gate (`_BlockingReviewPlan`) is held on an event for the whole call, so the start never waits on the gate in a passing run.

### Root cause (measured 2026-11-03)

Before returning the handle, the start path (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` `review_plan_start` -> `_start_gate_job`) runs work that builds the dedup key, all in an `anyio.to_thread` worker:

- `_plan_review_variant` -> `_material_key` -> `current_material_fingerprint` -> `rebar._reads.show_ticket` -> `ensure_fresh` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:193`): `git rev-parse` + a throttled `git fetch` of the tracker.
- `begin_gate_job` (`src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py`): `resolve_basis_sha` (`git rev-parse`) and `canonical_ticket_id` -> `tracker_dir` (`git rev-parse`).
- `record_gate_run` (index write) and `_spawn_gate_daemon` (thread start) cost under 5 ms.

That is 5 git child processes per start. The job id is derived from that key (basis SHA, canonical id, material fingerprint; bugs 3b27-8f4b and c912-f274 added the material part deliberately), so the work cannot move after the handle without redesigning dedup.

Phase timing at load average ~30, gate stubbed: material read 0.29-0.47 s, `begin_gate_job` 0.21-0.40 s, whole call 0.32-0.64 s.

Deterministic reproduction: a PATH shim that sleeps 0.45 s before exec'ing the real `git` makes the unchanged test fail at line 424 with `assert 2.478... < 2` and the same message, while the stub gate is still held. The start never waited on the gate; the bound measured git subprocess cost. So the defect is in the test oracle, not in production code: a wall-clock threshold measures host load together with the contract.

## Approach

Replace the elapsed-time bound with an ordering signal. That signal is exactly the contract ("the start returns while the gate is still running") and is independent of host speed:

1. `_BlockingReviewPlan` gains a `finished` event (set when the stub gate body returns) and a `hold` parameter (seconds its release wait lasts; default 5, unchanged for the other tests).
2. The test holds the gate with a generous `hold` (60 s) and releases it only after `review_plan_start` has returned. It captures `fake.finished.is_set()` at the moment the call returns and asserts it is False. A start that waits on the gate can only return after the stub's hold expires, so `finished` is already set and the assertion fails. A non-blocking start returns with the gate still held, however slow the host is.
3. Remove `anyio.fail_after(3)` and the `time.monotonic()` elapsed measurement from that test. The stub's own bounded hold prevents a deadlock, and the configured pytest-timeout (300 s, `pyproject.toml` `timeout = 300`) bounds any other hang.
4. A companion test proves the oracle detects the regression. It patches `rebar._mcp_llm.spawn_context_daemon` (imported at `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:16`, called at line 213) to run the daemon body inline, which is the "run the gate synchronously" mutant. It then asserts that the same ordering check reports the gate as finished before the start returned. That test uses a short `hold` (0.2 s), so it is fast and deterministic.

The scenario is shared between the 2 tests through a module-level helper in the test file. No `tests/_*.py` helper module, no autouse fixture, no new child processes.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py`: the stub, the rewritten test, the companion mutant test.

No production change: the pre-handle work is required to compute the dedup key.

## Testing

- Rewritten test passes on an unmodified start path, including with the 0.45 s slow-git shim on PATH (the shim run that failed before).
- Companion test passes: with the daemon spawn run inline, the ordering check reports the gate as finished before return.
- The rest of `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` and the MCP gate modules (`tests/unit/test_mcp_gate*.py`) still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The test proves "start does not wait for the gate" without an elapsed-time threshold: `grep -n "elapsed\|fail_after" tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` shows neither inside `test_review_plan_start_returns_a_handle_fast_then_polls_to_passed`, and the test passes.
- [x] The test fails when `review_plan_start` is changed to run the gate synchronously, and passes on main: `test_review_plan_start_ordering_check_flags_a_synchronous_gate` passes (the inline-spawn mutant is flagged), and the rewritten test passes with `PATH=<slow-git shim>:$PATH`, where the old test failed with `assert 2.478... < 2`.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py`, `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change lands through Gerrit at LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1; the change number and merged SHA are recorded as a ticket comment.
